title: Our Small Screens: A Bridge for Relationships, Not a Silent Wall
summary:
Imagine your little one smiling and cooing at a phone screen, while their grandmother responds with a smile and joy from afar. These fleeting moments, which we sometimes see as mere exceptions, are in fact golden opportunities to build bridges of warm relationships. You might feel anxious about screens, and this is a natural feeling, but the real difference lies in how they are used: Is it a window to a world your child interacts with, or just a silent broadcast that consumes their time without benefit?

The idea is not to ban screens entirely, but to transform them from a passive entertainment tool into a means of genuine communication. When your child interacts with someone they love through a video call, they are not just watching; they are participating. Their small brain receives real social cues: Grandma smiles, the child coos, and there is a mutual reaction. This two-way interaction, even if short, is fundamentally different from watching videos that require no participation from the child, and it contributes to building their social and emotional skills.

So, let's see short video calls as an opportunity to strengthen family bonds. Sit next to your child, name the person speaking, encourage them to wave and coo, and comment on the reactions. Make these moments short and focused, so that the screen becomes a means to strengthen the relationship, not just an entertainment screen. In this way, we protect our child's developing brain and nourish it with love and interaction, even across distances.
try_this: Tonight: Arrange a short video call (two minutes) with a relative your child loves. Sit next to your child, name the person, wave their hand, and comment on the relative's responses.
reflection_prompts: What difference did you notice in your child's interaction between a live video call and watching a recorded video?
How can I make any screen time (however short) an opportunity to strengthen relationships instead of silence?
parent_script: “Look, my darling, this is your grandma smiling at you! Let's wave to her.”
